movement_source: row 'Net profit after tax from continuing operations – cash basis', column FY25 (12 months ended Jun 2025) -> column FY26 (12 months ended Jun 2026)
headline: CBA's cash earnings (NPAT) increased $730 million (+7.1%) to $10,982 million in FY26. The growth was driven by a $1,563 million increase in Net Interest Income and a $196 million rise in Other Operating Income. These were partially offset by higher Underlying Operating Expenses ($719 million), an increase in Credit Impairment Charges ($62 million), and higher Tax expense ($208 million). Restructuring and notable items also increased by $40 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million (+7%) to $25,586 million, driven by volume growth of $92 billion in average interest earning assets, partly offset by a 3 bps decrease in NIM.

Other operating income rose $196 million (+4%) to $4,638 million, supported by increases in commissions ($135m), lending fees ($12m), funds management ($12m), and other income ($46m), partially offset by lower trading income (-$9m).

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million (+6%) to $13,585 million. This reflects higher staff expenses ($288m), IT services ($393m), and other expenses ($57m), partially offset by lower occupancy costs (-$19m).
Restructuring and notable items increased by $40 million to $170 million (FY25: $130 million), representing a negative contribution to earnings growth.

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million (+9%) to $788 million. The rise was primarily driven by Retail Banking Services (+$106m), partially offset by improvements in Business Banking (-$45m) and Institutional Banking (-$16m).

Corporate tax expense increased $208 million (+5%) to $4,699 million. This was driven by higher pre-tax profits, partially mitigated by a 50 bps decrease in the effective tax rate to 30.0% due to lower non-deductible expenses.

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items increased by $40 million year-on-year.
limitations: Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
